relevance_note: The paper reports eight HA20 patients with germline TNFAIP3 variants from three families: "Three TNFAIP3 variants, A547T, c.1906+2T>G, and R271X, were identified."
method_note: Read the full paper and Table 1 by hand; a short Python script in my scratch directory assembled the JSON from values I transcribed, and built Table 1 spans as verbatim row prefixes (checked against the table). Phenotype rows whose span is a Table 1 row prefix use the column header as feature text. Labels: probands use the paper's P-labels with pedigree IDs ('P1 (V:24)', 'P2 (III:5)', 'P3 (III:3)'); relatives use 'Family N' + pedigree ID because pedigree IDs repeat across families (IV:1 in Families 2 and 3; III:3 in Families 2 and 3). Table 1 rows carry only a pedigree number; rows were matched to people by sex and ages (row 1 = P1; rows 2-4, identical F/UN/>18, = P1's mother IV:14 and sisters V:22, V:26 in an order that cannot be determined but does not matter since the rows are identical; Family 2 'F 9 12' = daughter IV:1, 'F 15 35' = P2; Family 3 'M 15 40' = P3, 'F 8 10' = daughter IV:1). Contradictions: (1) P1 genital ulcers: text 'recurrent oral and genital ulcers from the age of 22' vs Table 1 Genital ulcers '–' (both rows emitted; checklist not reported). (2) P2 fever: text 'without recurrent fever' vs Table 1 Fever '+'; (3) Family 2 IV:1 fever: text 'recurrent fever' vs Table 1 Fever '–' (the fever cells look swapped between mother and daughter; both rows emitted for each; checklist not reported). (4) P3 autoantibodies: 'Blood tests for CBC, biochemistry panel, and autoantibodies were all normal' vs positive anti-TG/anti-TPO in text and Table 1 (both emitted; checklist not reported). (5) P3 age at onset: text 'oral ulcers since the age of 10' vs Table 1 onset 15 (text value recorded). (6) A547T pathogenicity: Abstract 'validated to be pathogenic' vs Discussion 'accurate pathogenic significance ... unknown'. Tensions resolved by judgement: P3 Table 1 Skin lesions '–' vs Henoch-Schonlein purpura at age 30 (checklist skin lesions set to not reported; HSP mapped to checklist vasculitis = observed); P3 Table 1 Genital ulcers '+' while the text describes only a 'perianal ulcer with an abscess' (recorded as stated in the table); P1 Table 1 Arthritis '+' while text says joint pain 'without joint swelling' (both recorded). Not used: post-treatment absence statements (e.g. P1 'did not exhibit fever, arthralgia, oral ulcers, or eye discomfort after a year of treatment'); the father IV:13's global 'no symptoms' was recorded as one excluded row but not propagated to checklist items; F1 III:2 and III:3 (only described as cousins of each other; 'grandmother' is not specified as maternal) were not given rows and consanguinity was left not reported; NOD2 variant not recorded for the father (paper says 'paternal' but does not report testing him). Variant inheritance for carrier relatives left not reported (rule 8): the paper shows a parent carries the variant but never states the origin. Family 2 cousins III:3/III:4: sex not stated, so 'no vulva ulcers' was not used to exclude checklist genital ulcers. P2 anaemia not mapped to 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' because no autoimmune cause is stated. Age at last evaluation recorded only for the two daughters (their text ages differ from or are separate from Table 1 diagnosis ages); probands' text ages equal Table 1 diagnosis ages and are recorded as age at diagnosis. Transcript NM_006290 for rows other than P1 comes from the Table 1 header 'TNFAIP3 variations (NM_006290)'; P1 text/figure give NM_006290.4. The literature review (126 patients, 35 articles) is aggregate only; no per-patient table, so no review rows.
